title: Content Writing — Practical Assessment
description: Professional Thought Leadership Write-up — a short professional piece (200-350 words) on a subject in your area of expertise.
instructions:
PROFESSIONAL CONTENT WRITING ASSESSMENT

Project: Professional Thought Leadership Write-up
Category: Content Writing
Format: Short Professional Write-up

1. PROJECT OVERVIEW

For this assessment, you are required to develop a well-researched, professionally written piece of content around a subject within your chosen area of expertise.

Your task is to demonstrate your ability to communicate ideas, share valuable insights, challenge common misconceptions, and establish professional authority through your writing.

You are expected to approach this task as a professional who understands the subject matter, not simply someone documenting information gathered from the internet.

2. TOPIC SELECTION

Choose ONE subject from the following professional areas:

- Personal Branding
- Digital Marketing
- Business Development
- Entrepreneurship
- Leadership and Management
- Career Development
- Customer Experience
- Financial Literacy
- Brand Strategy
- Productivity and Workplace Excellence
- Communication and Public Relations
- Sales and Business Growth

Your task is to identify a specific problem, misconception, overlooked opportunity, or recurring mistake within your chosen subject area and develop an insightful write-up around it.

You are not required to use the name of your chosen subject as your headline. Instead, create an original and highly compelling headline that captures the attention of your intended audience and makes them want to read further.

3. WRITING REQUIREMENTS

A. Compelling Headline
Your headline must:
- Capture attention immediately.
- Create curiosity or highlight a problem.
- Communicate the central idea of your write-up.
- Give your audience a reason to keep reading.

Avoid generic headlines that simply announce what the write-up is about.

B. Research & Subject Understanding
- Conduct proper research before writing.
- Gather relevant facts, insights, examples, and supporting information.
- Understand the subject matter beyond the information you find online.
- Ensure your arguments are logical, accurate, and relevant.
- Do not simply reproduce information from your research.

Your writing should demonstrate that you understand the subject and can communicate it from a professional perspective.

C. Audience Communication
- Identify a specific audience you are communicating with.
- Understand the problems, challenges, and questions that audience may have.
- Make your content relatable to their experiences.
- Ensure readers can recognise their own challenges within your writing.

Write to a particular audience, not everybody.

D. Writing Style & Tone
Your writing should:
- Sound professional, natural, and conversational.
- Have a one-on-one communication feel.
- Demonstrate confidence and clarity.
- Incorporate your own beliefs, perspectives, and professional opinions.
- Avoid sounding like a textbook, academic documentation, or a collection of bullet points.
- Maintain a consistent flow from beginning to end.

Your write-up should feel like a professional having a meaningful conversation with their audience.

E. Establishing Professional Authority
Your write-up should position you as someone who understands the subject deeply. You do not need to introduce yourself as an expert or tell readers how knowledgeable you are. Instead, demonstrate your understanding through:
- The quality of your insights.
- The strength of your arguments.
- The relevance of your examples.
- Your ability to identify problems and provide meaningful perspectives.
- The clarity with which you explain complex ideas.

F. Call to Action (CTA)
Your write-up must end with a strong call to action. Your CTA should encourage readers to engage with your content. You may encourage them to:
- Share their experiences.
- Contribute their opinions.
- Challenge or agree with your perspective.
- Share the write-up with someone who needs it.
- Take a specific action based on your message.

Avoid weak or generic closing statements. Make your CTA intentional and engaging.

4. IMPORTANT: ORIGINALITY & AI POLICY

This assessment is designed to evaluate your individual writing ability.

You are permitted to use AI tools and other research resources to:
- Explore your chosen subject.
- Understand unfamiliar concepts.
- Gather supporting information.
- Discover relevant industry insights.
- Verify facts and statistics.

However, you are NOT permitted to use AI to generate or write your submission.

All submissions will be screened using multiple AI-detection systems. Any submission flagged for AI-generated writing will be disqualified from grading.

Your ideas, thought process, writing, arguments, and final submission must be your own. Do not outsource your thinking to AI.

5. A NOTE ON RESEARCH AND WRITING

There is a difference between gathering information and understanding a subject.

We do not want a write-up that reads like a compilation of facts you found online. We want to see how you process information, connect ideas, form opinions, and communicate your understanding.

For example, when you discover a particular fact during research, don't just insert it into your writing because it sounds impressive. Understand what it means, why it matters, how it affects your audience, and what your professional interpretation of it is.

Your objective is not to show us how much information you can gather. It is to demonstrate how well you understand and communicate what you know.

6. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS

Your submission must include:
1. Your chosen professional subject.
2. Your intended target audience.
3. Your original, compelling headline.
4. Your completed professional write-up.
5. A strong closing CTA.
6. References or sources consulted during your research.

Recommended length: 200-350 words.

IMPORTANT NOTE ON LENGTH
This is a short professional write-up, NOT a full-length article. You are expected to communicate meaningful insights, demonstrate subject-matter understanding, and deliver value within a relatively short piece of writing.

Do not stretch your content unnecessarily to meet a word count. Every paragraph should contribute something meaningful to the overall message. We value depth of thought, clarity, originality, and resourcefulness over length.

Submit your write-up in the response box below (chosen subject, target audience, headline, the write-up itself, your CTA, and your references).

7. FINAL INSTRUCTIONS

Before submitting, ensure that:
- Your headline is compelling.
- Your audience is clearly defined.
- Your opening paragraph creates interest.
- Your arguments are clear and well-developed.
- Your writing demonstrates professional understanding.
- Your content has a natural conversational flow.
- Your perspectives and beliefs are evident.
- Your write-up ends with a strong CTA.
- Your work is original and properly researched.

Remember: Anyone can gather information and put it into paragraphs. The real skill of a professional content writer is the ability to understand information, develop meaningful perspectives, and communicate those perspectives in a way that influences how people think, feel, or act.

Good luck!
